# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (use instead of source text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE YELLOW HOUSE; MASTER OF MEN (E. Phillips Oppenheim; Gutenberg 41402; P.F. Collier 1912; vol. 1)

**Narrator/family:** Kate Ffolliot (narrator, pale, black-haired, lived abroad: school in Berlin & Heidelberg, Dresden; good Heidelberg degree; restless, sharp-tongued). Father: Rev. Horace Ffolliot, curate-in-charge at a northshire village (later Canon of Eastminster); tall, slim, clean-shaven, grey eyes, fastidious, sermons without notes; formerly at Belchester (suburban parish, "two curates"); Colonel Dacre complained to Bishop about his London trips. Sister: Alice Ffolliot, youngest, homely, literal, conventional, parish worker, "good girl". Servants: Mary (maid), Morris (gives letters). Vicarage has cedar tree, lawn, lane, plantation.

**Neighbors/places:** Deville Court (Bruce Deville's estate; "lord of the Manor of a dozen parishes"). Yellow House (odd little house through plantation, rented by Adelaide Fortress; front hall with Mudie's box; study with Burmese gong; Socialist). Naselton Hall (Lady Amy Naselton, middle-aged matchmaker, godmother of Bruce; husband; son Fred Naselton; Romneys, Lady Romney). Countess of Sysington/Applecorn; Holgates; Colonel Dacre; Mr. Hewitt (schools); Mr. Charlsworth (churchwarden); Harrison (tenant farmer, traps; Bruce's dogs incl. beagle Lawless, Marvel, Madam, Diana the horse, chestnut).

**Characters:**
- **Bruce Deville**: tall, broad, ragged beard, long hair, grey piercing eyes, shabby clothes, surly; cosmopolitan; spent 12 years abroad; spent fortune on singer Marie Leparte; poses as ruined; loves Kate; saved Olive in Swiss/Baeren carriage accident (stopped runaway horses, broke driver's leg); godmother Lady Naselton. Friend/ trustee of Adelaide (father Mr. Bromley Deville was her father's oldest friend).
- **Adelaide Fortress** (Marcia): Kate's mother; ~35-40, plain-ish, thin, brown hair with grey, dark eyes, socialist journalist, anti-marriage in youth; lived with Horace (then "Philip Maltabar") unmarried; he entered Church and left her; she took up with another man (the affair with "Marcia"). Kate learns she's daughter of Horace and Adelaide (ch. XIX).
- **Horace Ffolliot = "Philip Maltabar"** (earlier name). Killed Stephen Berdenstein (who attacked him with knife, wounded lung); confessed in ch. XXIX.
- **Stephen Berdenstein**: South American (Rio) returned man, wealthy; loved Adelaide; enemy of Philip Maltabar; found dead in plantation/ wood near Yellow House after Sunday evensong, body brought to churchyard; had revolver; in church shouted "Judas!" and died.
- **Olive Berdenstein**: sister of Stephen; short, dark, thin, sallow, white teeth, diamonds, sealskin coat; loves Bruce; wants Philip Maltabar punished; blackmail-ish offer of £10,000 (ch XXV); later goes to police station; in Eastminster denounces father; at Commercial Road she tries; finally forgives in Colville Hall.

**Other:** Canon Ffolliot; Bishop of Exchester; Mr. Densham (Socialist candidate); Lady Applecorn; Mr. Smith (detective); Mr. Hewitt.

**Key events in order:**
1. Lady Naselton's call; gossip about Yellow House woman and Bruce (ch I). Horace faints after hearing Bruce's voice (ch II).
2. Bruce meets Kate re Lawless beagle leg (ch III); Horace: "that man was closely associated with the most unhappy chapter."
3. Storm; Kate at Yellow House; Marcia's den; Bruce there; Horace bursts in, calls "Marcia!" and leaves (ch IV).
4. Horace leaves for London after South American letter ("London about the 15th"); Bruce drops letter with same handwriting (ch V).
5. Lady Naselton's party; Berdenstein (millionaire, "Rio", "Adelaide Fortress"; wants to regain her) (ch VI).
6. Horace missing; Kate confronts Bruce & Adelaide at Yellow House; Horace returns, with revolver (ch VII).
7. Sunday; Horace ill, walk to Downs with Kate; Berdenstein arrives, Horace takes him away (ch VIII).
8. Sermon "wages of sin"; dying Berdenstein at church door: "Judas!" (ch IX).
9. Kate ill ~1 week; Horace made canon; inquest "murder" (ch X).
10. Horace confesses to Kate partially; Kate promises silence (ch XI).
11. Olive Berdenstein visits (Maltabar); Horace refuses to see (ch XII-XIII).
12. Horace's wound (ch XIV); Olive shows photo in cabinet of "Philip Maltabar" = Horace (ch XV-XVI); Horace admits it (ch XVI).
13. Bruce, Adelaide; Kate reveals she is Adelaide's daughter; Horace's secret (ch XVII-XX).
14. Horace flees to London; telegram; Kate's removal to London as secretary (ch XXI-XXVII).
15. Olive's proposal to Kate: keep away from Bruce (ch XXII-XXIV).
16. Bruce proposes to Kate; she refuses (ch XXV). Later Bruce proposes again and she accepts (ch XXVIII).
17. Commercial Road sighting of Horace; telegram; Horace's letter from Ventnor (ch XXVII).
18. Eastminster: Olive confronts Horace; Horace confesses killing Stephen (ch XXIX).
19. Horace leaves; Colville Hall (East End) farewell; Horace dies: "This is happiness." (ch XXX).

**Notable quotes:** "Judas! you, Judas! Oh! my God!" ; "The wages of sin is death"; "This is happiness."; Ventnor letter signed "Horace Ffolliot."

**Transcriber notes:** typo corrections list (ch pages).

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE GREAT WHITE ARMY (Max Pemberton; Gutenberg 35540; Cassell 1916)

**Frame:** Author's note: Napoleon's Grand Army retreat from Moscow 1812; narrator = Surgeon-Major Janil de Constant (veteran, former Paris University professor, fled Paris 1792, studied medicine at Leipsic). Nephew: Captain Léon de Courcelles, of the Vélites of the Guard (white horse; handsome; womanizer). Other: Sergeant Bourgogne (Vélites), Sergeant Gustav Bardot (Fusiliers, "the antelope"), Gascogne (Léon's servant), Major Pavart (chasseurs), Sergeant Picard, Dumesnil, Murat, Ney, Eugène, Davout, Gros-Jean, Colonel Bourgoriau, Captain Payard (dragoons, cormorant), Major Duhesne, Captains Legard & Fournier.

**Chapters (titles):**
I. The Woman on the Stairs; II. The Guillotine; III. The Treasure in the Woods; IV. Phantom Music; V. The Camp by the River; VI. The Witch in Ermine; VII. Little Petrovka; VIII. The Affair at the Post-House; IX. We Cross the Bérézina; X. The Last Review.

**Ch I (Moscow, Sept 14 1812):** Janil enters Moscow; lackey Heriot (dandy, Paris 1790, snuff box) takes him into house of Prince Boris; dead youth (artist from Fréjus, shot in back); three convicts with torches; Janil knocks one down; on balcony; sees Valerie St. Antoine (sister of dead René/brother; father Colonel St. Antoine; prince's steward François killed brother); hidden chapel; convicts axe door; escape to cupola; Léon on white horse; palace fired; Janil blindfolded by Russian, Prince Nicholas (white uniform, black cuirass) rescues Valerie; Léon: "A welcome to Moscow!"

**Ch II (Moscow, Sept 28+):** Léon dines with Valerie at Ivan's round tower (Nicholas's house, island, drawbridge); Sergeant Bardot with Janil; gigantic dark feast; mock guillotine ("Dr. Guillotine"); Tartar executioner; Léon's speech "butchers are ennobled"; Bardot fires bell, cuts; Nicholas's arm severed at elbow by blade; Cossacks; Valerie found droshky; Léon asks "Where is Valerie St. Antoine?"

**Ch III (Oct 19 onward):** Retreat from Moscow; Zayde (Zoida), golden-haired girl with treasure of Prince Karasin (murdered elderly man/coachman in glade); monastery with monks (gilt dome); Léon wants to marry Zayde; drugged; monks flee; Janil and Léon attack monastery with cannon; no monks; chase by Cossacks; monks' bivouac fires fool Cossacks.

**Ch IV (Oct 29 snow; Slawkowo):** Wrecked yellow berline: Baroness de Nivois & granddaughter dead; Valerie alive; Valerie's father Colonel St. Antoine (chasseurs, Second Battalion) in Slawkowo church; Léon, Janil in blizzard; Sergeant Bourgogne's church; organist; friendly-fire massacre by chasseurs of line (~40 dead); Valerie burns Kutusoff plans; father dies at dawn; Napoleon threatens to shoot Janil if he doesn't bring Valerie; Valerie gone; Napoleon left with "a woman."

**Ch V (Camp by the River):** Captain Payard (dragoon, curly hair, blue eyes) takes Janil & Léon to Russian camp at village Vitzala; Madame Pauline (red hair, Cossack green uniform, lover of Colonel Ferdinand Tcharnhoff, dragoon); Tcharnhoff returns, threatens; Payard shot dead by Tcharnhoff; Pauline stabs Tcharnhoff; escape; wolves; Red Hussars rescue; Janil later met Pauline in Paris, Rue de Rivoli, June 1813.

**Ch VI (Liadoui, Nov):** Napoleon takes Janil to old Madame Zchekofsky's house near Liadoui; daughter Kyra (prophetess, claimed Moscow would burn), sleepwalking; Napoleon in chapel with Kyra; Cossacks; Janil impersonates Napoleon? (dons Napoleon's cloak & hat, feigns drunken laughter, "Ram ram" song); Cossack troop drunk; Janil awakes; Napoleon six leagues to Wilna; Zchekofsky later in Paris 1815.

**Ch VII (Little Petrovka, Nov 25):** Battle of Krasnoë; Emperor walks; Petrovka (girl disguised as soldier, golden hair, tall) leads Léon; farm of moujik Serges at Druobona; barn fire set by Anna (farmer's daughter); Petrovka tried by officers; Major Duhesne; hanging planned; Cossacks arrive (Petrovka's friends); spared; Petrovka: "do not forget little Petrovka."

**Ch VIII (Post-house, Nov 25 night):** Lost road near Bérézina; Cossacks; Léon kills Cossack leader; Janil wounded in arm; dying chasseur; Cossack capes; post-house; Valerie (in hussar uniform, "Imperatrice") there; Russian officers captured; Valerie reads Kutusoff aide's dispatch (bridge held); Marshal Ney sends Léon; young Jew Isidore & wife guide; robbers' cave; Léon/Janil kill robbers; Isidore keeps plunder; reach Bobr; Valerie rides out.

**Ch IX (Bérézina, Nov 26-28):** Borisoff; priest's house; Joan d'Izambert (14, silver fox fur); brother Gabriel d'Izambert (pontonnier, fever, ford discovery below Studianka); father General d'Izambert (engineer); Valerie stays; Emperor interviews; pontoons; ford; Russians bombard; bridge blown; Gabriel recalled to blow bridge; Janil, Valerie, Joan swim the river on horse; reach far bank; Gabriel drowning seen.

**Ch X (Last Review):** ~30,000 remain; Smorgoni (Napoleon leaves Dec 5 for Murat); Vilna; party: Valerie, Léon, Joan, Bardot, Janil; farmhouse of Poles (widow and two sons); attack; Bardot shot dead; flight; merry old gentleman (Polish nobleman, "Excellency") takes Valerie and Joan, prisoners to Elbing; prefect Herr Immo von Gustorf; prison; Valerie is "mistress" of prefect's house; Marshal Ney's last review; French frontier; "The day of battle was over; the night of our sorry victory had been won."

**Key quotes:** "the dead have come to life!"; "Dr. Guillotine"; "Let no man consider himself happy until he is dead."; "Ram, ram, ram, tam, Plan, tire-lire ram plan"; "Lucky devil."

**Transcription:** Gutenberg text; Cassell 1916 colophon.
